turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me know if I am too quiet.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: You are fine, thank you for asking.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: I drove her over, I will listen along.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What brings you to the clinic today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I came because of my chest.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it move into your arms or up toward your neck?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nowhere else.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How would you describe what you feel in your chest?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It feels like burning right behind the breastbone.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Did it begin suddenly or slowly?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It came on slowly last night.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you notice it when you exercise or exert yourself?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Only when I hurry.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I did not catch most of what the nurse told me earlier.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you for saying so. I will speak slowly and write down the main points.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does anything ease the pain when it is there?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nothing really helps.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Are you drenched or clammy during the episodes?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A little sweaty, yes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you blacked out at all?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, I almost passed out in the kitchen.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you feel winded along with the pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A little bit, yes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Has a parent or sibling had a heart attack?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nobody that I remember.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you have any history of diabetes, blood pressure problems or cholesterol problems, or do you smoke?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have high blood pressure, and I have diabetes. I have never smoked.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you have a history of heart surgery or stents?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, they did a heart bypass on me some years back.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Which pills do you take regularly?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take Lisinopril and Metformin.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: To finish, here is the plan. First, get a heart tracing and a blood test today. Second, call 911 if the pain gets worse or does not stop. To be sure I was clear, what will you do next?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I will get the heart tracing and the blood test today and call 911 if the pain gets worse or will not stop.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: I will write it down for her.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any other questions before you go?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nothing else, thank you.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: All right, we are done. Take care of yourself.
